faq.q: What kinds of product photos can I make?
faq.a: White background shots, lifestyle scenes, on-model photos, new backgrounds, feed ad images, and close-ups such as color variants or what's in the box. Each one starts from a photo of your product. For a listing, keep the main view simple enough to compare with other products.

faq.q: What kind of photo should I upload?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo where the whole product is visible and nothing is cut off at the edges. Even light and a plain background help, but a clear phone photo works too. Avoid reflections and filters that hide the product finish.

faq.q: Which product photo type should I make first?
faq.a: Start with a clean product view for the listing. Add a lifestyle, detail, on-model, or feed image when shoppers need context or a closer look. Use context only after the basic shape and color are clear. Check the crop on mobile before you publish it, because small details can disappear at feed width.

faq.q: Can I put a price or sale text on the photo?
faq.a: Add text after you download. Canva works well for prices, discount codes, and headlines. AI-generated lettering can contain typos, so typing it yourself keeps it accurate. Keep legal offer wording outside the generated image.

faq.q: Can I keep my logo or packaging text?
faq.a: You can ask for visible marks to stay, but generated lettering can shift. Start from a close, sharp source image and compare the result with the item you ship; add exact packaging wording in your editor when it must be correct.

faq.q: Can I show an item in use?
faq.a: Yes. Describe a believable hand or person interaction that helps shoppers understand the item. A natural hand or person can make scale easier to judge.

faq.q: How many views should a small product listing have?
faq.a: Start with a clear primary view, then add one context scene and one useful detail or worn view. Choose the next image based on a real shopper question such as scale, fit, texture or how the item is used. A detail view can answer texture or closure questions without replacing the hero.

faq.q: What size and crop should a product photo use?
faq.a: The photo hub makes square images by default. Keep the full product inside the source frame, then check the square crop on mobile so handles, straps, lids, and small details do not disappear at feed width.

items.d: Leave the whole item in frame and avoid props touching its edges, especially for mugs, candles, and small home goods.
